question.text: Three members of the Medici family went on to hold which office in Rome, taking the names Leo X, Clement VII and Leo XI?
question.answerHtml: Pope [or “the papacy;” or Supreme Pontiff; or Pontifex Maximus; or Bishop of Rome]
question.clue: The last Englishman to hold it was Nicholas Breakspear.

swap.text: Which Catholic religious order, founded by Ignatius Loyola and nicknamed “God’s Marines”, counted the missionary Francis Xavier among its members?
swap.clue: Two of its members prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk.

question.text: Which pope founded World Youth Day in 1985? His visit to his home country helped inspire the Solidarity movement, which went on to end communist rule there.
question.clue: He visited Mehmet Ali Agca in prison to forgive him for trying to kill him.

swap.text: In 2013, which pope became the first since 1294 to resign?
swap.answerHtml: Pope Benedict XVI [prompt on Benedict; or Joseph Aloisius Ratzinger]
swap.clue: Critics called him “the pope of aesthetics” for his lavish dress, and he had been conscripted into Germany’s military in the Second World War.

question.text: What name is given to the meeting in which the College of Cardinals is shut away in the Vatican to choose a pope, its name referring to being locked in “with a key”?
question.clue: Since 1996 the cardinals taking part have stayed in Saint Martha’s House rather than on rented cots behind cloth partitions.

swap.text: Which order of knights first based itself at the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, and was dissolved by the pope in the early 14th century after Philip IV of France accused it of fraud and heresy?
swap.answerHtml: Knights Templar [or Templars; or Templiers; or Poor Fellow-Soldiers of Christ and of the Temple of Solomon; or Pauperes commilitones Christi Templique Salomonici; or Order of the Temple; or Ordre du Temple]
swap.clue: After winning the Battle of Hattin, Saladin bought and executed its members en masse.

question.text: Which pope launched the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont, offering remission of sins to those who joined and supposedly declaring “Deus vult” – “God wills it”?
question.clue: He allied himself with Roger I of Sicily and was heavily influenced by a delegation from Alexios I Komnenos.

swap.text: During the 14th century a series of popes lived in which city in the south of modern-day France?
swap.clue: Six papal elections were held in its Palais des Papes.

question.text: Which pope, who led the Church during the Second World War, has been called “Hitler’s Pope” for not doing enough to stop the Holocaust?
question.clue: At his trial, Karl Wolff testified that he had been ordered to kidnap this pope.

swap.text: Which order of crusading knights captured the island of Rhodes from the Byzantines and made it their base, and still exists today?
swap.answerHtml: Knights Hospitallers [or Hospitallers; or Knights of St John; or Order of St John; or Knights of Malta]
swap.clue: Founded by the Blessed Gerard, it held the fortresses of Margat and Krak des Chevaliers before being forced from the Holy Land.

question.text: The period when the popes lived at Avignon is sometimes called by what name, borrowed from the exile of the Jews from Judah begun by Nebuchadnezzar and ended by Cyrus the Great?
question.clue: The name refers to a period of exile in the Old Testament.

swap.text: Born Ugo Buoncompagni, which pope called for Queen Elizabeth I to be deposed, but is better remembered for the calendar named after him?
swap.clue: He had Aloysius Lilius and Christopher Clavius design the system, and brought it in with the bull Inter gravissimas.

question.text: Which church council elected Pope Martin V, ending the Western Schism, and had the theologian Jan Hus burned at the stake?
question.clue: It was called by Emperor Sigismund, and it canonized St Bridget of Sweden.

swap.text: Which pope moved the papacy to Avignon and suppressed the Knights Templar at the Council of Vienne?
swap.clue: He rescinded an earlier papal bull which proclaimed that there is no salvation outside the Church.

question.text: Persuaded by St Catherine of Siena, which pope moved the papacy back to Rome?
question.answerHtml: Pope <u>Gregory XI</u> [or Pierre-Roger de <u>Beaufort</u>; prompt on “<u>Gregory</u>”]
question.clue: He hired John Hawkwood to fight on his behalf in the War of the Eight Saints.

swap.text: Which church council of 1409 tried and failed to end the Western Schism, and was superseded by a later council?
swap.clue: It elected Philargi as Alexander V, but both rival popes refused to recognise it.

question.text: Which 14th-century pope, opposed by the antipope Clement VII during the Western Schism, once complained that he couldn’t hear enough screaming while rebellious cardinals were being tortured?
question.clue: He probably died of injuries from a painful fall from his mule at Narni.

swap.text: What grim name is given to the event at which Pope Stephen VI put the rotting corpse of his predecessor Formosus on trial, then had it thrown into the Tiber?
swap.clue: Held in 897, it grew out of tension between Spoletan and Roman factions over whether Arnulf or Lambert should be Holy Roman Emperor.

question.text: Which pope, introduced to Arabic numerals while studying at a Catalonian monastery, is credited with reintroducing the abacus and the armillary sphere to Europe?
question.clue: The first French pope, he took his name from the pope said by the forged Donation of Constantine to have been given power over the Western Roman Empire.

swap.text: Which pope, elected after an 18-month vacancy following Celestine IV, called the Council of Lyons that excommunicated Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II?
swap.clue: He enticed Henry III to take the throne of Sicily.
